title.zh: 卷45 列傳第37 儒林
title.raw: 卷45 列傳第37 儒林 Volume 45 Biographies 37: Confucian Scholars

sentences.zh: 盧誕 盧光 沈重 樊深 熊安生 樂遜

translations.literal: Lu Dan, Lu Guang, Shen Zhong, Fan Shen, Xiong Ansheng, Yue Xun
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dan, Lu Guang, Shen Zhong, Fan Shen, Xiong Ansheng, and Yue Xun

sentences.zh: 自書契之興，先哲可得而紀者，莫不備乎經傳。

translations.literal: From the rise of writing, the former sages who can be recorded—none are not fully preserved in the classics and commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Since the advent of writing, every sage of old whose deeds could be recorded has been fully preserved in the classics and their commentaries.

sentences.zh: 若乃選君德於列辟，觀遺烈於風聲，帝莫高於堯、舜，王莫顯於文、武。

translations.literal: When one selects rulerly virtue among the feudal lords and observes their lasting achievements in renown, no emperor is higher than Yao and Shun, no king more illustrious than Wen and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When one weighs the moral stature of rulers among the feudal lords and reads their enduring legacy in the fame they left behind, no emperors stand higher than Yao and Shun, and no kings shine more brightly than King Wen and King Wu.

sentences.zh: 是以聖人祖述其道，垂文於六學；

translations.literal: Therefore the sages traced and transmitted the Way, leaving writings in the six disciplines;
translations.idiomatic: That is why the sages took up and handed down the Way, setting their teachings down in the six classical disciplines;

sentences.zh: 憲章其教，作範於百王。

translations.literal: they took their teaching as law and model, making a standard for the hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: they enshrined that teaching as law and example, establishing a model for kings through the ages.

sentences.zh: 自茲以降，三微驟遷，五紀遞襲，損益異術，治亂殊塗。

translations.literal: From this time downward, the three minima shifted swiftly, the five cycles succeeded one another, increase and decrease followed different methods, order and disorder took separate paths.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, the three minima shifted in rapid succession, the five cycles replaced one another, methods of reform and retrenchment diverged, and the roads to order and to chaos parted.

sentences.zh: 秦承累世之基，任刑法而殄滅；

translations.literal: Qin inherited the foundation of many generations, relied on penal law, and perished;
translations.idiomatic: Qin inherited a foundation built over many generations, yet trusted in penal law and was destroyed;

sentences.zh: 漢無尺土之業，崇經術而長久。

translations.literal: Han had no patrimony of even a foot of earth, honored classical learning, and endured long.
translations.idiomatic: Han began without even a foot of territory to its name, yet exalted classical learning and endured for ages.

sentences.zh: 雕蟲是貴，魏道所以陵夷；

translations.literal: When ornamental writing was prized, the Way of Wei therefore declined;
translations.idiomatic: When ornamental verse was prized above all, the moral way of Wei declined;

sentences.zh: 玄風旣興，晉綱於焉大壞。

translations.literal: Once the abstruse current arose, the framework of Jin was thereby greatly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Once the fashion for abstruse discourse took hold, the foundations of Jin were thoroughly undone.

sentences.zh: 考九流之殿最，校四代之興衰，正君臣，明貴賤，美教化，移風俗，莫尚於儒。

translations.literal: Examining the ranking of the nine schools, comparing the rise and fall of the four ages, rectifying ruler and minister, clarifying noble and base, beautifying instruction and transformation, shifting customs and mores—nothing is more honored than Confucianism.
translations.idiomatic: When one weighs the standing of the nine schools, compares the rise and fall of four dynasties, sets ruler and minister in their proper relation, clarifies noble and base, refines education, and shifts customs and mores, nothing ranks above the Confucian way.

sentences.zh: 故皇王以之致刑措而反淳朴，賢達以之鏤金石而雕竹素。

translations.literal: Therefore emperors and kings through it achieved the laying aside of punishments and a return to plain simplicity; worthies and eminent men through it carved metal and stone and inscribed bamboo and silk.
translations.idiomatic: That is how emperors and kings brought punishments to rest and returned the realm to plain simplicity, and how worthies and men of distinction engraved their words on metal and stone and inscribed them on bamboo and silk.

sentences.zh: 儒之時義大矣哉！

translations.literal: How great is the timely significance of Confucianism!
translations.idiomatic: How vast is the timely significance of the Confucian teaching!

sentences.zh: 自有魏道消，海內版蕩，彝倫攸斁，戎馬生郊。

translations.literal: From the time the Way of Wei faded, within the seas the land was in turmoil, constant norms were destroyed, and war-horses were born in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the moral way of Wei faded, the realm was thrown into turmoil, the constant norms of human relations were shattered, and war-horses bred even in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 先王之舊章，往聖之遺訓，掃地盡矣。

translations.literal: The old statutes of the former kings and the bequeathed instructions of past sages were swept clean to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The old statutes of former kings and the bequeathed teachings of past sages were swept away entirely.

sentences.zh: 及太祖受命，雅好經術。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor received the Mandate, he greatly loved classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor received the Mandate, he had a deep love for classical learning.

sentences.zh: 求闕文於三古，得至理於千載，黜魏、晉之制度，復姬旦之茂典。

translations.literal: He sought missing texts in the three antiquities, obtained the supreme principle from a thousand years, dismissed the institutions of Wei and Jin, and restored the flourishing canons of the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sought out lost texts from the three antiquities, recovered the supreme principle from a thousand years of tradition, set aside the institutions of Wei and Jin, and restored the full ritual canon of the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 盧景宣學通羣藝，修五禮之缺；

translations.literal: Lu Jingxuan's learning penetrated all the arts; he repaired the gaps in the five rites;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jingxuan mastered every branch of learning and repaired what was missing in the five rites;

sentences.zh: 長孫紹遠才稱洽聞，正六樂之壞。

translations.literal: Changsun Shaoyuan's talent was called comprehensive knowledge; he corrected the damage to the six kinds of music.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Shaoyuan was famed for comprehensive learning and set right what had been ruined in the six kinds of court music.

sentences.zh: 由是朝章漸備，學者向風。

translations.literal: From this the court regulations gradually became complete, and scholars turned toward the wind.
translations.idiomatic: From this the court's institutions gradually took full shape, and scholars turned toward the new order.

sentences.zh: 世宗纂曆，敦尚學藝。

translations.literal: The Shizong succeeded to the calendar and earnestly honored learning and the arts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, he earnestly promoted learning and the arts.

sentences.zh: 內有崇文之觀，外重成均之職。

translations.literal: Within there was the Hall for Honoring Literature; without, weight was placed on the duties of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace stood the Hall for Honoring Literature; without, the duties of the Imperial Academy were given great weight.

sentences.zh: 握素懷鈆重席解頤之士，間出於朝廷；

translations.literal: Men who grasped the unadorned and cherished the lead stylus, of the sort who fill heavy seats and loosen chins in debate, appeared from time to time at court;
translations.idiomatic: Scholars who held the unadorned text and the writing stylus in hand—men of the sort who fill the teacher's seat and set their listeners' chins wagging in debate—appeared at court from time to time;

sentences.zh: 圓冠方領執經負笈之生，著錄於京邑。

translations.literal: Students in round caps and square collars, holding the classics and bearing satchels, were entered in the registers of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Students in round caps and square collars, clutching their classics and shouldering their satchels, were enrolled in the registers of the capital.

sentences.zh: 濟濟焉足以踰于向時矣。

translations.literal: In such abundance they were sufficient to surpass former times.
translations.idiomatic: In such numbers they were more than enough to surpass former times.

sentences.zh: 洎高祖保定三年，乃下詔尊太傅燕公為三老。

translations.literal: By the third year of Baoding under Emperor Gaozu, an edict was issued honoring the Grand Tutor, Duke of Yan, as one of the Three Elders.
translations.idiomatic: By the third year of the Baoding era under Emperor Gaozu, an edict was issued honoring the Grand Tutor, Duke of Yan, as one of the Three Elders.

sentences.zh: 帝於是服袞冕，乘碧輅，陳文物，備禮容，清蹕而臨太學。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon donned the dragon robes and cap, rode the green carriage, displayed the ritual implements, prepared full ceremonial demeanor, cleared the road with insignia, and proceeded to the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon donned the dragon robes and ceremonial cap, rode the green imperial carriage, displayed the ritual regalia, arrayed the full ceremonial retinue, cleared the road with insignia, and proceeded in person to the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 袒割以食之，奉觴以酳之。

translations.literal: He bared his shoulder and cut meat to feed him, raised a goblet and rinsed his mouth for him.
translations.idiomatic: He bared his shoulder and cut meat to serve him, then raised a goblet and offered the rinsing cup in the rite of respect.

sentences.zh: 斯固一世之盛事也。

translations.literal: This was indeed a grand event of an age.
translations.idiomatic: This was truly a grand event of the age.

sentences.zh: 其後命輶軒以致玉帛，徵沈重於南荊。

translations.literal: Afterward he ordered light carriages to bear jade and silks and summoned Shen Zhong from southern Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he dispatched light carriages bearing jade and silks and summoned Shen Zhong from southern Jing.

sentences.zh: 及定山東，降至尊而勞萬乘，待熊生以殊禮。

translations.literal: When the east of the mountains was pacified, he lowered the supreme honor to comfort one who commanded ten thousand chariots, and treated Master Xiong with exceptional ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When the east of the mountains was pacified, he humbled the supreme throne to honor a man who had once commanded ten thousand chariots, and treated Master Xiong with exceptional ceremony.

sentences.zh: 是以天下慕嚮，文教遠覃。

translations.literal: Therefore the realm looked up in admiration, and civil teaching spread far.
translations.idiomatic: The whole realm looked up in admiration, and civil culture spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 衣儒者之服，挾先王之道，開黌舍延學徒者比肩；

translations.literal: Those who wore the robes of scholars, carried the Way of the former kings, and opened schoolhouses to receive pupils stood shoulder to shoulder;
translations.idiomatic: Men who wore the scholar's robe, carried the Way of the former kings, and opened schoolhouses to take on pupils stood shoulder to shoulder;

sentences.zh: 勵從師之志，守專門之業，辭親戚甘勤苦者成市。

translations.literal: those who encouraged the will to follow teachers, kept to a single specialty, left kin, and accepted hardship filled the marketplaces.
translations.idiomatic: those who steeled their resolve to follow a teacher, held to a single specialty, left kin behind, and embraced hardship filled the towns like a marketplace.

sentences.zh: 雖遺風盛業，不逮魏、晉之辰，而風移俗變，抑亦近代之美也。

translations.literal: Although the lingering wind and flourishing achievement did not reach the age of Wei and Jin, yet the shift of custom and change of mores were nevertheless a beauty of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: Although the lingering glory of that age did not match the height of Wei and Jin, the shift in customs and mores was nevertheless a fine achievement of recent times.

sentences.zh: 其儒者自有別傳及終於隋之中年者，則不兼錄。

translations.literal: Confucian scholars who already have separate biographies or who died in the middle years of Sui are not included together here.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian scholars who already have separate biographies, or who died in the middle years of Sui, are not included here.

sentences.zh: 自餘撰於此篇云。

translations.literal: The remainder are set forth in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The rest are recorded in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 盧誕，范陽涿人也，本名恭祖。

translations.literal: Lu Dan was a man of Zhuo in Fanyang; his original name was Gongzu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dan was a native of Zhuo in Fanyang commandery; his original name was Gongzu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖晏，博學善隸書，有名於世。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yan was broadly learned and skilled in clerical script, and had a name in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yan was broadly learned and skilled in clerical script, and was famed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 仕燕為給事黃門侍郎、營丘成週二郡守。

translations.literal: He served Yan as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and as administrator of the two commanderies of Yingqiu and Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Yan state as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and as administrator of the commanderies of Yingqiu and Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖壽，太子洗馬。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shou was Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shou served as Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 燕滅入魏，為魯郡守。

translations.literal: When Yan was destroyed he entered Wei and became administrator of Lu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan fell he entered Wei service and became administrator of Lu commandery.

sentences.zh: 父叔仁，年十八，州辟主簿。

translations.literal: His father Shuren, at eighteen, was summoned by the province as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuren, at the age of eighteen, was summoned by the province to serve as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，除員外郎。

translations.literal: He was recommended as a xiucai and appointed Outer Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as a xiucai and appointed Outer Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以親老，乃辭歸就養。

translations.literal: Because his parents were old, he resigned and returned home to support them.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents grew old, he resigned and returned home to care for them.

sentences.zh: 父母旣歿，哀毀六年，躬營墳壟，遂有終焉之志。

translations.literal: After his parents had died, he mourned in devastation for six years, personally built their tombs, and thus formed the resolve to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: After his parents died, he mourned in deepest grief for six years, built their tombs with his own hands, and resolved to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 魏景明中，被徵入洛，授威遠將軍、武賁中郎將，非其好也。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era of Wei he was summoned to Luoyang and given the posts of General Who Establishes Might and Central Commander of the Martial Guard—neither was to his liking.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingming era of Wei he was summoned to Luoyang and given the posts of General Who Establishes Might and Central Commander of the Martial Guard—neither suited his taste.

sentences.zh: 尋除鎮遠將軍、通直散騎常侍，竝稱疾不朝。

translations.literal: Soon he was made General Who Pacifies the Distance and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; for both he pleaded illness and did not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made General Who Pacifies the Distance and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; for both posts he pleaded illness and refused to attend court.

sentences.zh: 乃出為幽州司馬，又辭歸鄉里。

translations.literal: He was then sent out as marshal of You province, and again resigned and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent out as marshal of You province, but again resigned and returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 當時咸稱其高尚焉。

translations.literal: At the time all praised his lofty integrity.
translations.idiomatic: At the time everyone praised his lofty integrity.

sentences.zh: 誕幼而通亮，博學有詞彩。

translations.literal: Dan from youth was penetrating and bright, broadly learned and gifted in literary expression.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was penetrating and bright from childhood, broadly learned, and gifted in literary expression.

sentences.zh: 郡辟功曹，州舉秀才，不行。

translations.literal: The commandery summoned him as merit officer; the province recommended him as xiucai—he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery summoned him as merit officer and the province recommended him as xiucai, but he declined both.

sentences.zh: 起家侍御史，累遷輔國將軍、太中大夫、幽州別駕、北豫州都督府長史。

translations.literal: He began his career as attendant censor and was promoted in succession to General Who Assists the State, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, chief assistant of You province, and chief clerk of the North Yu regional headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as attendant censor and rose in succession to General Who Assists the State, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, chief assistant of You province, and chief clerk of the North Yu regional headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時刺史高仲密以州歸朝，朝廷遣大將軍李遠率軍赴援，誕與文武二千餘人奉候大軍。

translations.literal: At the time the inspector Gao Zhongmi surrendered the province to the court; the court sent the great general Li Yuan with an army to aid him, and Dan with more than two thousand civil and military officials went out to receive the army.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the inspector Gao Zhongmi surrendered the province to the court; the court sent the great general Li Yuan with an army to support him, and Dan went out with more than two thousand civil and military officials to receive the army.

sentences.zh: 以功授鎮東將軍、金紫光祿大夫，封固安縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was given General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, enfeoffed as Baron of Gu'an with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and enfeoffed as Baron of Gu'an with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋加散騎侍郎，拜給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry and appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally made Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry and appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 魏帝詔曰：「經師易求，人師難得。

translations.literal: The Emperor of Wei issued an edict saying: "A teacher of the classics is easy to find; a teacher of men is hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor of Wei issued an edict saying, "A teacher of the classics is easy to find, but a teacher of men is hard to obtain.

sentences.zh: 朕諸兒稍長，欲令卿為師。

translations.literal: My sons are gradually growing; I wish to have you as their teacher.
translations.idiomatic: My sons are growing up, and I wish to appoint you as their teacher.

sentences.zh: 」於是親幸晉王第，敕晉王以下，皆拜之於帝前。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he personally visited the residence of the Prince of Jin and ordered the prince and those below him all to bow to him before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he personally visited the residence of the Prince of Jin and ordered the prince and all his younger brothers to bow to him in the emperor's presence.

sentences.zh: 因賜名曰誕。

translations.literal: He thereupon bestowed the name Dan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon bestowed on him the name Dan.

sentences.zh: 加征東將軍、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was additionally made General Who Pacifies the East and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made General Who Pacifies the East and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 太祖又以誕儒宗學府，為當世所推，乃拜國子祭酒。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor also, because Dan was a Confucian patriarch of the academy of learning and was esteemed by the age, appointed him Director of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor also, because Dan was a leading Confucian scholar of the academy and was esteemed throughout the realm, appointed him Director of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 進車騎大將軍，儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry with precedence equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry with precedence equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，除秘書監。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 盧光字景仁，小字伯，范陽公辯之弟也。

translations.literal: Lu Guang, courtesy name Jingren, childhood name Bo, was the younger brother of the Duke of Fanyang, Gong Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guang, whose courtesy name was Jingren and childhood name Bo, was the younger brother of the Duke of Fanyang, Gong Bian.

sentences.zh: 性溫謹，博覽羣書，精於《三禮》，善陰陽，解鐘律，又好玄言。

translations.literal: His nature was mild and careful; he broadly read all books, was expert in the Three Rites, skilled in yin-yang lore, understood pitch pipes and musical scales, and also loved abstruse discourse.
translations.idiomatic: He was mild and careful by nature, read widely in all books, was expert in the Three Rites, skilled in yin-yang lore, understood pitch pipes and musical scales, and also loved abstruse discourse.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，釋褐司空府參軍事，稍遷明威將軍、員外侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang he doffed his commoner's garb as staff officer of the Ministry of Works, and was gradually promoted to General of Illustrious Might and Outer Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiaochang era he entered office as a staff officer of the Ministry of Works and was gradually promoted to General of Illustrious Might and Outer Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，光于山東立義，遙授大都督、晉州刺史、安西將軍、銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Guang raised a loyal force in Shandong and was appointed from afar as Grand Commander, inspector of Jin province, General Who Pacifies the West, and Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Guang raised a loyal force in Shandong and was appointed from afar as Grand Commander, inspector of Jin province, General Who Pacifies the West, and Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 光性崇佛道，至誠信敬。

translations.literal: Guang by nature revered Buddhism and the Way, with utmost sincerity and reverent respect.
translations.idiomatic: Guang revered Buddhism and the Way by nature, with utmost sincerity and reverent devotion.

sentences.zh: 嘗從太祖狩於檀臺山。

translations.literal: He once accompanied the Grand Ancestor on a hunt at Tantai Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He once accompanied the Grand Ancestor on a hunt at Tantai Mountain.

sentences.zh: 時獵圍旣合，太祖遙指山上謂羣公等曰：「公等有所見不？

translations.literal: At the time the hunting enclosure had closed; the Grand Ancestor pointed from afar to the mountain and said to the assembled lords and others: "Do you gentlemen see anything?
translations.idiomatic: The hunting enclosure had already closed when the Grand Ancestor pointed toward the mountain and asked the assembled lords, "Do any of you see anything?

sentences.zh: 」咸曰：「無所見。

translations.literal: " All said: "We see nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " They all said, "We see nothing.

sentences.zh: 」光獨曰：「見一桑門。

translations.literal: " Guang alone said: "I see a Buddhist monk.
translations.idiomatic: " Guang alone said, "I see a Buddhist monk.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「是也。

translations.literal: " The Grand Ancestor said: "That is so.
translations.idiomatic: " The Grand Ancestor said, "That is so.

sentences.zh: 」即解圍而還。

translations.literal: " He immediately lifted the enclosure and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately lifted the enclosure and turned back.

sentences.zh: 令光于桑門立處造浮圖，掘基一丈，得瓦缽、錫杖各一。

translations.literal: He ordered Guang to build a pagoda at the spot where the monk had stood; when they dug the foundation one zhang deep, they obtained one earthen bowl and one tin staff.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Guang to build a pagoda at the spot where the monk had stood; when they dug the foundation one zhang deep, they found one earthen bowl and one tin staff.

sentences.zh: 太祖稱歎，因立寺焉。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor praised this in wonder and thereupon established a monastery there.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor marveled at this and thereupon established a monastery there.

sentences.zh: 及為京兆，而郡舍先是數有妖怪，前後郡將無敢居者。

translations.literal: When he became administrator of Jingzhao, the commandery residence had previously had several demonic occurrences, and none of the successive commandery chiefs dared to live there.
translations.idiomatic: When he became administrator of Jingzhao, the commandery residence had long been haunted, and none of his predecessors had dared to live there.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「吉凶由人，妖不妄作。

translations.literal: Guang said: "Fortune and misfortune depend on men; demons do not act without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "Fortune and misfortune depend on men; demons do not act without cause.

sentences.zh: 」遂入居之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon entered and lived there.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon moved in.

sentences.zh: 未幾，光所乘馬忽升廳事，登床南首而立；

translations.literal: Before long, the horse Guang rode suddenly ascended to the main hall, climbed onto the bed, and stood facing south;
translations.idiomatic: Before long, the horse Guang rode suddenly entered the main hall, climbed onto the bed, and stood facing south;

sentences.zh: 又食器無故自破。

translations.literal: and again the food vessels broke for no reason.
translations.idiomatic: and his food vessels broke for no apparent reason.

sentences.zh: 光並不以介懷。

translations.literal: Guang did not take any of this to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Guang paid none of it any mind.

sentences.zh: 其精誠守正如此。

translations.literal: His sincere devotion and upright steadfastness were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the sincerity and steadfast integrity of his character.

sentences.zh: 撰《道德經章句》，行於世。

translations.literal: He compiled Exegetical Sections of the Daodejing, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Exegetical Sections on the Daodejing, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子賁嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ben succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ben succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 大象中，開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Daxiang era he was made General-in-Chief with the Grand Precedence of the Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daxiang era he was made General-in-Chief with the Grand Precedence of the Opening Office.

sentences.zh: 沈重字德厚，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Zhong, courtesy name Dehou, was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhong, whose courtesy name was Dehou, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 性聰悟，有異常童。

translations.literal: His nature was intelligent and perceptive; he was an extraordinary child.
translations.idiomatic: He was intelligent and perceptive by nature, an extraordinary child.

sentences.zh: 弱歲而孤，居喪合禮。

translations.literal: He was orphaned in early youth and observed mourning in accord with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in early youth, he observed mourning in full accord with ritual.

sentences.zh: 及長，專心儒學，從師不遠千里，遂博覽羣書，尤明《詩》、《禮》及《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: When grown, he devoted himself to Confucian learning, followed teachers without shunning a journey of a thousand li, and thus broadly read all books, especially mastering the Odes, the Rites, and the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he devoted himself to Confucian learning and would travel a thousand li to follow a teacher; he read widely in all books and was especially expert in the Odes, the Rites, and the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 梁大通三年，起家王國常侍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong of Liang he began his career as regular attendant of a princely kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Datong era of Liang he entered office as regular attendant of a princely kingdom.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝欲高置學官，以崇儒教。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang wished to set learning officials in high posts to honor Confucian teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang wished to elevate the status of learning officials in order to honor Confucian teaching.

sentences.zh: 中大通四年，乃革選，以重補國子助教。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong the selection was reformed, and Zhong was appointed assistant instructor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Zhongdatong era the selection system was reformed, and Zhong was appointed assistant instructor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 大同二年，除《五經》博士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong he was made Erudite of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Datong era he was made Erudite of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝之在藩也，甚歎異之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was in his princely fief, he greatly admired him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was still in his princely fief, he greatly admired him.

sentences.zh: 及即位，乃遣主書何武迎重西上。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he sent the chief clerk He Wu to welcome Zhong westward.
translations.idiomatic: When he ascended the throne, he sent the chief clerk He Wu to escort Zhong westward to court.

sentences.zh: 及江陵平，重乃留事梁主蕭詧，除中書侍郎，兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, Zhong remained to serve the Liang ruler Xiao Cha and was made Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat, concurrently Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, Zhong remained to serve the Liang ruler Xiao Cha and was made Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat, concurrently serving as Secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 累遷員外散騎侍郎、廷尉卿，領江陵令。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Outer Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry and Minister of Justice, and concurrently held the magistracy of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Outer Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry and Minister of Justice, while concurrently serving as magistrate of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 還拜通直散騎常侍、都官尚書，領羽林監。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Scattered Cavalry and Minister of Justice, and concurrently held the office of Director of the Feathered Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Scattered Cavalry and Minister of Justice, while concurrently serving as director of the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 察又令重於合歡殿講《周禮》。

translations.literal: Cha again had Zhong lecture on the Rites of Zhou in the Hall of Shared Joy.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha again had Zhong lecture on the 《Rites of Zhou》 in the Hall of Shared Joy.

sentences.zh: 高祖以重經明行修，乃遣宣納上士柳裘至梁徵之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, because Zhong's classical learning was clear and his conduct cultivated, dispatched the Superior Gentleman for Proclaiming Reception Liu Qiu to Liang to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhong's classical learning was clear and his conduct exemplary, Emperor Gaozu dispatched the superior gentleman for proclaiming reception Liu Qiu to Liang to summon him.

sentences.zh: 仍致書曰：

translations.literal: He also sent a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a letter that read:

sentences.zh: 皇帝問梁都官尚書沈重。

translations.literal: The Emperor inquires of Shen Zhong, Minister of Justice of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor inquires of Shen Zhong, Minister of Justice of Liang.

sentences.zh: 觀夫八聖六君，七情十義，殊方所以會軌，異代於是率由。

translations.literal: Observing the eight sages and six rulers, the seven emotions and ten righteousnesses—from distant regions they thereby align to the same track, in different ages they thereby follow the same path.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the eight sages and six rulers, the seven emotions and ten righteousnesses: from distant regions all alike converge on the same path, and in different ages all follow the same course.

sentences.zh: 莫不趣大順之遙塗，履中和之盛致。

translations.literal: None failed to hasten along the distant road of great accord and tread the full attainment of central harmony.
translations.idiomatic: None failed to hasten along the distant road of great accord or to tread the full attainment of central harmony.

sentences.zh: 及青緗起焰，素篆從風，文逐世疏，義隨運舛，大禮存於玉帛之間，至樂形於鐘鼓之外。

translations.literal: When the blue bindings flared up and plain bamboo slips followed the wind, writing grew sparse with the age and meaning went awry with the times; great ritual survived only among jade and silks, and supreme music took form only beyond bells and drums.
translations.idiomatic: Once the blue bindings caught fire and plain bamboo slips scattered on the wind, writing grew thin with the age and meaning went awry with the times; great ritual survived only as jade and silks, and supreme music appeared only beyond bells and drums.

sentences.zh: 雖分蛇、聚緯，鬱鬱之辭蓋闕；

translations.literal: Although there were the divided serpent and gathered weft, the lush phrasing was largely lacking;
translations.idiomatic: Although the age of divided serpents and gathered weft had its writers, the lush phrasing of true learning was largely gone;

sentences.zh: 當塗、典午，抑抑之旨無聞。

translations.literal: under the regency of Cao and the house of Jin, the restrained and solemn message was no longer heard.
translations.idiomatic: under the Cao regency and the Jin house, the restrained and solemn message was no longer heard.

sentences.zh: 有周開基，爰蹤聖哲，拯蒼生之已淪，補文物之將墜。

translations.literal: When Zhou opened its foundation, it traced the sages and wise men, rescued the black-haired people already sunk in ruin, and repaired the cultural artifacts about to fall.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou laid its foundation, it followed in the footsteps of the sages, rescued the people already sunk in ruin, and repaired the cultural heritage about to fall away.

sentences.zh: 天爵具修，人紀咸理。

translations.literal: The heavenly ranks were fully restored, and human norms were all set in order.
translations.idiomatic: The heavenly ranks were fully restored, and the norms of human conduct were all set in order.

sentences.zh: 朕寅奉神器，恭惟寶闕。

translations.literal: I reverently receive the sacred vessel and respectfully contemplate the treasured palace.
translations.idiomatic: I reverently hold the sacred vessel of rule and contemplate with awe the throne I have inherited.

sentences.zh: 常思復禮殷周之年，遷化唐虞之世。

translations.literal: I constantly think of restoring the ritual age of Yin and Zhou and transforming the realm to the era of Tang and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: I constantly think of restoring the ritual age of Yin and Zhou and transforming the realm to the era of Tang and Yu.

sentences.zh: 懼三千尚乖於治俗，九變未叶於移風。

translations.literal: I fear that the three thousand rules still fall short of governing custom, and the nine transformations have not yet harmonized with shifting the wind of mores.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that the three thousand rules of ritual still fall short of governing custom, and that the nine transformations of music have not yet harmonized with shifting the wind of mores.

sentences.zh: 欲定畫一之文，思杜二家之說。

translations.literal: I wish to fix a uniform text and think of the doctrines of the two Du families.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to establish a uniform canon of learning and seek the doctrines of the two Du families.

sentences.zh: 知卿學冠儒宗，行標士則。

translations.literal: I know that your learning crowns the Confucian patriarchs and your conduct marks the standard for scholars.
translations.idiomatic: I know that your learning crowns the Confucian school and your conduct marks the standard for scholars.

sentences.zh: 卞寶復潤於荊陰，隨照更明於漢浦。

translations.literal: The jade of Bian would again be moistened in the shade of Jing; the pearl of Sui would shine more brightly on the banks of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: The jade of Bian would again be moistened in the shade of Jing; the pearl of Sui would shine more brightly on the banks of the Han.

sentences.zh: 是用寤寐增勞，瞻望軫念。

translations.literal: For this reason my waking and sleeping increase in labor, and in looking up I am filled with anxious thought.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason I labor waking and sleeping, and look toward you with anxious longing.

sentences.zh: 爰致束帛之聘，命翹車之招。

translations.literal: I therefore send the gift of bundled silks and command the summons of the high-wheeled carriage.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore send the gift of bundled silks and command the summons carried by the high-wheeled carriage.

sentences.zh: 所望鳳舉鴻翻，俄而萃止。

translations.literal: What I hope is that you will rise like a phoenix and soar like a wild goose, and soon gather and alight here.
translations.idiomatic: What I hope is that you will rise like a phoenix and soar like a wild goose, and soon arrive to settle here.

sentences.zh: 明斯隱滯，合彼異同。

translations.literal: Clarify what is hidden and stagnant; harmonize what differs and agrees.
translations.idiomatic: Clarify what has been hidden and neglected; harmonize what has diverged and what agrees.

sentences.zh: 上庠弗墜於微言，中經罔闕於逸義。

translations.literal: The upper academy would not let subtle words fall; the central classics would lack no neglected meanings.
translations.idiomatic: The upper academy would not let subtle teachings fall away, and the central classics would lack no neglected meanings.

sentences.zh: 近取無獨善之譏，遠應有兼濟之美。

translations.literal: In the near term one would avoid the reproach of cultivating goodness alone; in the long term one would answer to the beauty of benefiting all together.
translations.idiomatic: In the near term you would avoid the reproach of cultivating goodness for yourself alone; in the long term you would fulfill the ideal of benefiting all together.

sentences.zh: 可不盛歟。

translations.literal: Could this not be magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Would this not be magnificent!

sentences.zh: 昔申涪鮐背，方辭東國；

translations.literal: Formerly Shenzi of Piao, with his back bent like a dried fish, was just leaving the eastern state;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Shenzi of Piao, bent with age like a dried fish, was just leaving the eastern state;

sentences.zh: 公孫黃發，始造西京。

translations.literal: Gongsun with his yellow hair was first coming to the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: and Gongsun Hong, white-haired with age, was first coming to the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 遂使道為藝基，功參治本。

translations.literal: They thereby made the Way the foundation of the arts and their achievement joined the root of governance.
translations.idiomatic: They thereby made the Way the foundation of learning and their achievement joined the root of governance.

sentences.zh: 今者一徵，諒兼其二。

translations.literal: Now a single summons surely combines both of these.
translations.idiomatic: A single summons now surely combines both of these.

sentences.zh: 若居形聲而去影響，尚迷邦而忘觀國，非所謂也。

translations.literal: If one dwells in form and sound yet departs from shadow and echo, still clings to one's state yet forgets to observe the realm—this is not what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: If you dwell in form and sound yet turn away from shadow and echo, still cling to your state yet forget to observe the realm as a whole—that is not what is meant.

sentences.zh: 又敕襄州總管、衛公直敦喻遣之，在途供給，務從優厚。

translations.literal: He also ordered the regional commander of Xiang province, Duke Wei Zhi, earnestly to instruct and send him on his way, with supplies on the road to be as generous as possible.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the regional commander of Xiang province, Duke Wei Zhi, earnestly to instruct and escort him, with supplies on the road to be as generous as possible.

sentences.zh: 保定末，重至于京師。

translations.literal: At the end of Baoding, Zhong arrived again at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Baoding era, Zhong arrived again at the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔令討論《五經》，幷校定鐘律。

translations.literal: An edict ordered discussion of the Five Classics and, together with this, correction and fixing of pitch pipes and musical scales.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered discussion of the 《Five Classics》 and, together with this, the correction and fixing of pitch pipes and musical scales.

sentences.zh: 天和中，復於紫極殿講三教義。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era he again lectured on the doctrines of the three teachings in the Hall of Purple Apex.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianhe era he again lectured on the doctrines of the three teachings in the Hall of Purple Apex.

sentences.zh: 朝士、儒生、桑門、道士至者二千餘人。

translations.literal: Court officials, Confucian scholars, Buddhist monks, and Daoist priests who came numbered more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: More than two thousand court officials, Confucian scholars, Buddhist monks, and Daoist priests attended.

sentences.zh: 重辭義優洽，樞機明辯，凡所解釋，咸為諸儒所推。

translations.literal: Zhong's phrasing and meaning were graceful and thorough, his pivotal reasoning clear and discriminating; all his explanations were esteemed by the various Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's phrasing was graceful and his reasoning clear; all his explanations were esteemed by the Confucian scholars present.

sentences.zh: 六年，授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、露門博士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was given General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Precedence of the Opening Office with precedence equal to the Three Excellencies, and Erudite of the Dew Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made General of Agile Cavalry, granted the Grand Precedence of the Opening Office with precedence equal to the Three Excellencies, and appointed Erudite of the Dew Gate.

sentences.zh: 仍於露門館為皇太子講論。

translations.literal: He continued to lecture and discuss for the crown prince at the Dew Gate Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to lecture for the crown prince at the Dew Gate Academy.

sentences.zh: 建德末，重自以入朝旣久，且年過時制，表請還梁。

translations.literal: At the end of Jiande, Zhong himself, because he had been at court already a long time and his years exceeded the proper limit, submitted a memorial requesting to return to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jiande era, Zhong himself, having been at court for many years and exceeded the proper age limit, submitted a memorial requesting to return to Liang.

sentences.zh: 高祖優詔答之曰：「開府漢南杞梓，每軫虛衿；

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu replied with a gracious edict saying: "You, Opening Office, are a catalpa and paulownia of south of the Han; I constantly bend my empty breast to you;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu replied with a gracious edict saying, "You, Opening Office, are a catalpa and paulownia of the lands south of the Han; I constantly bend my empty breast to you;

sentences.zh: 江東竹箭，亟疲延首。

translations.literal: a bamboo arrow of the east of the river—I have long been weary with craning my neck in expectation.
translations.idiomatic: a bamboo arrow of the lands east of the river—I have long wearied myself craning my neck in expectation.

sentences.zh: 故束帛聘申，蒲輪徵伏。

translations.literal: Therefore I sent bundled silks to summon Shen and a rush-wheeled carriage to invite Fu.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I sent bundled silks to summon Shenzi and a rush-wheeled carriage to invite Gongsun Hong.

sentences.zh: 加以梁朝舊齒，結綬三世，沐浴榮光，祗承寵渥，不忘戀本，深足嘉尚。

translations.literal: Added to this, as an old retainer of the Liang court, tied to office for three generations, bathed in glory and reverently receiving favor, you do not forget your attachment to your roots—this is deeply worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Added to this, as an old retainer of the Liang court, tied to office for three generations, bathed in glory and reverently receiving favor, you do not forget your attachment to your roots—this is deeply worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 而楚材晉用，豈無先哲。

translations.literal: Yet Chu talent used in Jin—was there not a former sage?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chu talent employed in Jin—was there not a precedent among the sages?

sentences.zh: 方事求賢，義乖來肅。

translations.literal: I am just now seeking the worthy; the principle runs counter to your coming to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: I am just now seeking the worthy; the principle runs counter to your coming to pay your respects and leave.

sentences.zh: 」重固請，乃許焉。

translations.literal: " Zhong firmly requested again, and he was then permitted.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhong firmly requested again, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 遣小司門上士楊

translations.literal: He dispatched the Superior Gentleman of the Junior Gate Office Yang
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched the superior gentleman of the junior gate office Yang

translations.literal: (note)
translations.idiomatic: (editorial note)

sentences.zh: 〔汪〕送之。

translations.literal: [Wang] to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: [Wang] to escort him.

sentences.zh: 梁主蕭巋拜重散騎常侍、太常卿。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler Xiao Kui appointed Zhong Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler Xiao Kui appointed Zhong Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 大象二年，來朝京師。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daxiang he came to court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Daxiang era he came to court at the capital.

sentences.zh: 開皇三年，卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaihuang he died, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Kaihuang era he died, at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝遣舍人蕭子寶祭以少牢，贈使持節、上開府儀同三司、許州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui sent the Attendant Gentleman Xiao Zibao to sacrifice with the secondary victims, and posthumously gave him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Upper Grand Precedence of the Opening Office with precedence equal to the Three Excellencies, and inspector of Xu province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui sent the attendant gentleman Xiao Zibao to offer sacrifice with the secondary victims, and posthumously granted him the staff of authority, upper grand precedence of the opening office with precedence equal to the Three Excellencies, and the post of inspector of Xu province.

sentences.zh: 重學業該博，為當世儒宗。

translations.literal: Zhong's learning was comprehensive and broad; he was the Confucian patriarch of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's learning was comprehensive and broad; he was the leading Confucian scholar of his age.

sentences.zh: 至於陰陽圖緯，道經釋典，靡不畢綜。

translations.literal: As for yin-yang lore, charts and weft texts, Daoist classics and Buddhist scriptures—none was he not fully versed in.
translations.idiomatic: As for yin-yang lore, charts and weft texts, Daoist classics and Buddhist scriptures, there was none in which he was not fully versed.

sentences.zh: 又多所撰述，咸得其指要。

translations.literal: He also wrote many works, all grasping the essential points.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote many works, all of which grasped the essential points.

sentences.zh: 其行於世者，《周禮義》三十一卷、《儀禮義》三十五卷、《禮記義》三十卷、《毛詩義》二十八卷、《喪服經義》五卷、《周禮音》一卷、《儀禮音》一卷、《禮記音》二卷、《毛詩音》二卷。

translations.literal: Those circulating in the world were: Meaning of the Rites of Zhou in thirty-one juan, Meaning of the Ceremonial Rites in thirty-five juan, Meaning of the Record of Rites in thirty juan, Meaning of the Mao Odes in twenty-eight juan, Meaning of the Classic of Mourning Garments in five juan, Pronunciation of the Rites of Zhou in one juan, Pronunciation of the Ceremonial Rites in one juan, Pronunciation of the Record of Rites in two juan, and Pronunciation of the Mao Odes in two juan.
translations.idiomatic: Those circulating in the world were: 《Meaning of the Rites of Zhou》 in thirty-one juan, 《Meaning of the Ceremonial Rites》 in thirty-five juan, 《Meaning of the Record of Rites》 in thirty juan, 《Meaning of the Mao Odes》 in twenty-eight juan, 《Meaning of the Classic of Mourning Garments》 in five juan, 《Pronunciation of the Rites of Zhou》 in one juan, 《Pronunciation of the Ceremonial Rites》 in one juan, 《Pronunciation of the Record of Rites》 in two juan, and 《Pronunciation of the Mao Odes》 in two juan.

sentences.zh: 樊深字文深，河東猗氏人也。

translations.literal: Fan Shen, courtesy name Wenshen, was a man of Yishi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shen, whose courtesy name was Wenshen, was a native of Yishi in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 早喪母，事繼母甚謹。

translations.literal: He lost his mother early and served his stepmother with great care.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother early and served his stepmother with great care.

sentences.zh: 弱冠好學，負書從師於三河，講習《五經》，晝夜不倦。

translations.literal: At the capping age he loved learning, shouldered his books and followed teachers in Sanhe, lectured and studied the Five Classics, day and night without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: At the capping age he loved learning, shouldered his books and followed teachers in Sanhe, and studied the 《Five Classics》 day and night without weariness.

sentences.zh: 魏永安中，隨軍征討，以功除蕩寇將軍，累遷伏波、征虜將軍，中散大夫。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era of Wei he followed the army on campaign, and for merit was made General Who Sweeps Away Bandits; he was promoted in succession to General Who Pacifies the Waves and General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yong'an era of Wei he followed the army on campaign and, for his merit, was made General Who Sweeps Away Bandits; he rose in succession to General Who Pacifies the Waves and General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 嘗讀書見吾丘子，遂歸侍養。

translations.literal: Once in reading he came upon Master Wuqiu and thereupon returned home to serve and support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Once while reading he came upon the story of Master Wuqiu and thereupon returned home to serve and support his parents.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，樊、王二姓舉義，為東魏所誅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, the Fan and Wang clans raised a loyal force and were executed by Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, the Fan and Wang clans raised a loyal force and were executed by Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 深父保周、叔父歡周並被害。

translations.literal: Shen's father Baozhou and his uncle Huanzhou were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's father Baozhou and his uncle Huanzhou were both killed.

sentences.zh: 深因避難，墜崖傷足，絕食再宿。

translations.literal: Shen, while fleeing hardship, fell from a cliff and injured his foot, and went without food for two nights.
translations.idiomatic: While fleeing the turmoil, Shen fell from a cliff and injured his foot, and went without food for two nights.

sentences.zh: 於後遇得一簞餅，欲食之；

translations.literal: Later he came upon a basket of cakes and wished to eat them;
translations.idiomatic: Later he came upon a basket of cakes and wished to eat them;

sentences.zh: 然念繼母年老患痹，或免虜掠，乃弗食。

translations.literal: but thinking that his stepmother was old and afflicted with paralysis, she might escape capture by the enemy, he did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: but thinking that his aged stepmother, afflicted with paralysis, might still escape capture, he did not eat.

sentences.zh: 夜中匍匐尋母，偶得相見，因以饋母。

translations.literal: In the night he crawled on hands and knees seeking his mother, chanced to meet her, and therefore gave the food to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the night he crawled on hands and knees seeking his mother, chanced to find her, and gave her the food.

sentences.zh: 還復遁去，改易姓名，遊學于汾、晉之間，習天文及算曆之術。

translations.literal: He returned and fled again, changed his name, traveled and studied between Fen and Jin, and learned astronomy and the arts of calculation and calendrics.
translations.idiomatic: He fled again, changed his name, traveled and studied between Fen and Jin, and learned astronomy and the arts of calculation and calendrics.

sentences.zh: 後為人所告，囚送河東。

translations.literal: Later he was reported by someone, imprisoned, and sent to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone reported him; he was imprisoned and sent to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 屬魏將韓軌長史張曜重其儒學，延深至家，因是更得逃隱。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhang Yao, chief clerk to the Wei general Han Gui, valued his Confucian learning and invited Shen to his home; thereby he was able to escape and hide again.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Zhang Yao, chief clerk to the Wei general Han Gui, valued his Confucian learning and invited Shen to his home; thereby he was able to escape and hide again.

sentences.zh: 太祖平河東，贈保周南郢州刺史，歡周儀同三司。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor pacified Hedong, he posthumously gave Baozhou the post of inspector of Southern Ying province and Huanzhou precedence equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor pacified Hedong, he posthumously gave Baozhou the post of inspector of Southern Ying province and Huanzhou precedence equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 深歸葬其父，負土成墳。

translations.literal: Shen returned to bury his father, carrying earth on his back to form the tomb mound.
translations.idiomatic: Shen returned to bury his father, carrying earth on his back to form the tomb mound.

sentences.zh: 尋而于謹引為其府參軍，令在館教授子孫。

translations.literal: Soon Yu Jin brought him in as staff officer of his headquarters and had him in the residence teaching his sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yu Jin brought him in as a staff officer of his headquarters and had him teach his sons and grandsons in the residence.

sentences.zh: 除撫軍將軍、銀青光祿大夫，遷開府屬，轉從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon, moved to staff of the opening office, and transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon, moved to staff of the opening office, and transferred to attendant gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 謹拜司空，以深為諮議。

translations.literal: When Jin was appointed Minister of Works, he made Shen his adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Jin was appointed Minister of Works, he made Shen his adviser.

sentences.zh: 大統十五年，行下邽縣事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Datong he acted as magistrate of Xiaqi county.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Datong he acted as magistrate of Xiaqi county.

sentences.zh: 太祖置學東館，教諸將子弟，以深為博士。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor established the Eastern Hall school to teach the sons and grandsons of the generals, and made Shen an erudite.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor established the Eastern Hall school to teach the sons and grandsons of the generals, and made Shen an erudite.

sentences.zh: 深經學通贍，每解書，嘗多引漢、魏以來諸家義而說之。

translations.literal: Shen's classical learning was penetrating and ample; whenever he explained a text, he often cited the interpretations of various schools from Han and Wei onward.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's classical learning was penetrating and ample; whenever he explained a text, he often cited the interpretations of various schools from Han and Wei onward.

sentences.zh: 故後生聽其言者，不能曉悟。

translations.literal: Therefore the younger students who heard his words could not understand clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the younger students who heard his lectures could not follow him clearly.

sentences.zh: 皆背而譏之曰：「樊生講書多門戶，不可解。

translations.literal: They all turned their backs and mocked him, saying: "Master Fan lectures on texts with too many schools—he cannot be understood.
translations.idiomatic: They all turned their backs and mocked him, saying, "Master Fan lectures with too many schools of interpretation—nothing can be understood.

sentences.zh: 」然儒者推其博物。

translations.literal: " Yet the Confucians esteemed his broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet the Confucian scholars esteemed his broad learning.

sentences.zh: 性好學，老而不怠。

translations.literal: His nature loved learning, and in old age he did not slacken.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning by nature and did not slacken even in old age.

sentences.zh: 朝暮還往，常據鞍讀書，至馬驚墜地，損折支體，終亦不改。

translations.literal: Morning and evening coming and going, he constantly read while seated in the saddle; when his horse was startled and he fell to the ground, breaking his limbs, he still did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening, coming and going, he constantly read while seated in the saddle; when his horse was startled and he fell to the ground, breaking his limbs, he still did not change.

sentences.zh: 後除國子博士，賜姓万紐於氏。

translations.literal: Later he was made erudite of the Imperial University and granted the surname Wanniu in the Yu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made erudite of the Imperial University and granted the surname Wanniu in the Yu clan.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜大學助教，遷博士，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: When the six offices were established, he was appointed assistant instructor of the Grand Academy, promoted to erudite, and given General of Chariots and Cavalry with precedence equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When the six offices were established, he was appointed assistant instructor of the Grand Academy, promoted to erudite, and given General of Chariots and Cavalry with precedence equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，遷縣伯中大夫，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe he was moved to Grand Master of the County Baron rank and given the Grand Precedence of the Opening Office with precedence equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhe he was promoted to grand master of the county baron rank and given the grand precedence of the opening office with precedence equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 建德元年，表乞骸骨，詔許之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiande he submitted a memorial requesting to retire on account of old bones, and an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiande he submitted a memorial requesting retirement, and an edict permitted it.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有疑議，常召問焉。

translations.literal: When the court had doubtful matters for discussion, he was often summoned to be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: When the court had doubtful matters for discussion, he was often summoned for consultation.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 深旣專經，又讀諸史及《蒼雅》、篆籀、陰陽、卜筮之書。

translations.literal: Shen, having specialized in the classics, also read the various histories and books such as the Cangjie glossary, seal and zhoushu scripts, yin-yang lore, and divination.
translations.idiomatic: Having specialized in the classics, Shen also read the various histories and books such as the 《Cangjie Glossary》, seal and zhoushu scripts, yin-yang lore, and divination.

sentences.zh: 學雖博贍，訥於辭辯，故不為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Although his learning was broad and ample, he was slow in eloquent debate, and therefore was not praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Although his learning was broad and ample, he was slow in eloquent debate and therefore was not widely praised in his own time.

sentences.zh: 撰《孝經》、《喪服問疑》各一卷，撰《七經異同說》三卷、《義

translations.literal: He compiled one juan each of the Classic of Filial Piety and Questions and Doubts on Mourning Garments, and compiled three juan of Discussions of Differences among the Seven Classics and Meaning of the
translations.idiomatic: He compiled one juan each of the 《Classic of Filial Piety》 and 《Questions and Doubts on Mourning Garments》, and compiled three juan of the 《Discussions of Differences among the Seven Classics》 and 《Meaning of the

translations.literal: (Classics)
translations.idiomatic: (Classics [in the received text])

sentences.zh: 〔綱〕畧論》幷

translations.literal: [Outline] Summary Treatise, together with
translations.idiomatic: [Outline] Summary Treatise, together with

translations.literal: (month)
translations.idiomatic: (month [in the received text])

sentences.zh: 《〔目〕錄》三十一卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: the [Catalog] in thirty-one juan—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: the 《[Catalog]》 in thirty-one juan—all circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 熊安生字植之，長樂阜城人也。

translations.literal: Xiong Ansheng, courtesy name Zhizhi, was a man of Fucheng in Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Ansheng, whose courtesy name was Zhizhi, was a native of Fucheng in Changle commandery.

sentences.zh: 少好學，勵精不倦。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and strove with tireless spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved learning and strove with tireless spirit.

sentences.zh: 初從陳達受《三傳》，又從房虯受《周禮》，並通大義。

translations.literal: At first he received the Three Commentaries from Chen Da, and also received the Rites of Zhou from Fang Qiu, mastering the great meaning of both.
translations.idiomatic: At first he studied the 《Three Commentaries》 under Chen Da, and also studied the 《Rites of Zhou》 under Fang Qiu, mastering the great meaning of both.

sentences.zh: 後事徐遵明，服膺歷年。

translations.literal: Later he served Xu Zunming and held him close to his breast for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Later he studied under Xu Zunming and held him in devoted esteem for many years.

sentences.zh: 東魏天平中，受《禮》於李寶鼎。

translations.literal: During Tianping of Eastern Wei, he received the Rites from Li Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era of Eastern Wei, he studied the Rites under Li Baoding.

sentences.zh: 遂博通《五經》。

translations.literal: Thereupon he attained thorough mastery of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he attained thorough mastery of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 然專以《三禮》教授。

translations.literal: Yet he specialized in teaching the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he specialized in teaching the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 弟子自遠方至者，千餘人。

translations.literal: Disciples who came from distant regions numbered more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Disciples who came from distant regions numbered more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 乃討論圖緯，捃摭異聞，先儒所未悟者，皆發明之。

translations.literal: He then deliberated on charts and weft texts, gathered and collected unusual accounts, and clarified everything that previous Confucians had failed to comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: He then deliberated on charts and weft texts, gathered obscure accounts, and clarified everything that earlier Confucians had failed to grasp.

sentences.zh: 齊河清中，陽休之特奏為國子博士。

translations.literal: During Heqing of Qi, Yang Xiuzhi specially memorialized that he be made Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: During the Heqing era of Northern Qi, Yang Xiuzhi specially memorialized that he be appointed Erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷旣行《周禮》，公卿以下多習其業，有宿疑礩滯者數十條，皆莫能詳辨。

translations.literal: At that time the court had already adopted the Rites of Zhou; from ministers and dukes downward many had studied its disciplines, yet there were several dozen long-standing doubts and stubborn difficulties that none could explain in detail.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court had already adopted the Rites of Zhou; from ministers and dukes downward many had studied its disciplines, yet there were several dozen long-standing doubts and stubborn difficulties that none could explain in detail.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，齊請通好，兵部尹公正使焉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe, Qi requested friendly relations, and Yin Gongzheng of the Ministry of War was sent as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Tianhe era, Qi requested friendly relations, and Yin Gongzheng of the Ministry of War was sent as envoy.

sentences.zh: 與齊人語及《周禮》，齊人不能對。

translations.literal: When he spoke with the men of Qi about the Rites of Zhou, the men of Qi could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke with the men of Qi about the Rites of Zhou, the men of Qi could not reply.

sentences.zh: 乃令安生至賓館與公正言。

translations.literal: They thereupon ordered Ansheng to go to the guest quarters and speak with Gongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: They thereupon ordered Ansheng to go to the guest quarters and speak with Gongzheng.

sentences.zh: 公正有口辯，安生語所未至者，便撮機要而驟問之。

translations.literal: Gongzheng was skilled in debate; wherever Ansheng's discourse had not yet reached, he would seize on the crucial points and question him abruptly.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzheng was skilled in debate; wherever Ansheng's discourse had not yet reached, he would seize on the crucial points and question him abruptly.

sentences.zh: 安生曰：「禮義弘深，自有條貫。

translations.literal: Ansheng said, "The rites and their meaning are vast and profound; they have their own order and thread.
translations.idiomatic: Ansheng said, "The rites and their meaning are vast and profound; they have their own order and thread.

sentences.zh: 必欲升堂睹奧，寧可汩其先後。

translations.literal: If one truly wishes to ascend the hall and behold the inner sanctum, how can one muddy the sequence of first and after?
translations.idiomatic: If one truly wishes to ascend the hall and behold the inner sanctum, how can one muddy the sequence of first and after?

sentences.zh: 但能留意，當為次第陳之。

translations.literal: If you only pay heed, I shall set them forth in proper order.
translations.idiomatic: If you only pay heed, I shall set them forth in proper order.

sentences.zh: 」公正於是具問所疑，安生皆為一一演說，咸究其根本。

translations.literal: " Gongzheng thereupon set forth all his doubts in full; Ansheng expounded each one in turn, all tracing to their roots.
translations.idiomatic: " Gongzheng thereupon set forth all his doubts in full; Ansheng expounded each one in turn, all tracing to their roots.

sentences.zh: 公正深所嗟服，還，具言之于高祖。

translations.literal: Gongzheng was deeply impressed and admiring; upon returning, he recounted it all to Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzheng was deeply impressed and admiring; upon returning, he recounted it all to Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖大欽重之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu greatly esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 及高祖入鄴，安生遽令掃門。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu entered Ye, Ansheng immediately ordered the gate swept.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu entered Ye, Ansheng immediately ordered the gate swept.

sentences.zh: 家人怪而問之，安生曰：「周帝重道尊儒，必將見我矣。

translations.literal: His household wondered and asked why; Ansheng said, "The Zhou emperor values the Way and honors the Confucians—he is sure to come see me.
translations.idiomatic: His household wondered and asked why; Ansheng said, "The Zhou emperor values the Way and honors the Confucians—he is sure to come see me.

sentences.zh: 」俄而高祖幸其第，詔不聽拜，親執其手，引與同坐。

translations.literal: " Before long Emperor Gaozu visited his residence; an edict forbade him to bow, and the emperor personally took his hand and drew him to sit together.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long Emperor Gaozu visited his residence; an edict forbade him to bow, and the emperor personally took his hand and drew him to sit together.

sentences.zh: 謂之曰：「朕未能去兵，以此為愧。

translations.literal: He said to him, "I have not yet been able to lay down arms, and take this as a matter of shame.
translations.idiomatic: He said to him, "I have not yet been able to lay down arms, and take this as a matter of shame.

sentences.zh: 」安生曰：「黃帝尚有阪泉之戰，況陛下龔行天罰乎。

translations.literal: " Ansheng said, "Even the Yellow Emperor still had the battle at Banquan—how much the more when Your Majesty carries out Heaven's punishment with righteous authority!
translations.idiomatic: " Ansheng said, "Even the Yellow Emperor still had the battle at Banquan—how much the more when Your Majesty carries out Heaven's punishment with righteous authority!

sentences.zh: 」高祖又曰：「齊氏賦役繁興，竭民財力。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu also said, "The Qi regime imposed taxes and corvée in profusion, exhausting the people's wealth and strength.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Gaozu also said, "The Qi regime imposed taxes and corvée in profusion, exhausting the people's wealth and strength.

sentences.zh: 朕救焚拯溺，思革其弊。

translations.literal: I have rescued those in fire and saved those drowning, and wish to reform these abuses.
translations.idiomatic: I have rescued those in fire and saved those drowning, and wish to reform these abuses.

sentences.zh: 欲以府庫及三臺雜物散之百姓，公以為何如？

translations.literal: I wish to distribute the treasury stores and the sundry goods of the Three Platforms among the common people—what do you think of this?
translations.idiomatic: I wish to distribute the treasury stores and the sundry goods of the Three Platforms among the common people—what do you think of this?

sentences.zh: 」安生曰：「昔武王克商，散鹿臺之財，發鉅橋之粟。

translations.literal: " Ansheng said, "In olden days King Wu conquered Shang, scattered the wealth of Lutai, and released the grain at Jutiao.
translations.idiomatic: " Ansheng said, "In olden days King Wu conquered Shang, scattered the wealth of Lutai, and released the grain at Jutiao.

sentences.zh: 陛下此詔，異代同美。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's edict shares the same excellence across different ages.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's edict shares the same excellence across different ages.

sentences.zh: 」高祖又曰：「朕何如武王？

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu also said, "How do I compare to King Wu?
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Gaozu also said, "How do I compare to King Wu?

sentences.zh: 」安生曰：「武王伐紂，縣首白旗；

translations.literal: " Ansheng said, "King Wu punished Zhou, hung his head upon a white banner;
translations.idiomatic: " Ansheng said, "King Wu punished Zhou, hung his head upon a white banner;

sentences.zh: 陛下平齊，兵不血刃。

translations.literal: Your Majesty pacified Qi without blood staining the blades.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty pacified Qi without blood staining the blades.

sentences.zh: 愚謂聖畧為優。

translations.literal: I deem your sage strategy the superior one.
translations.idiomatic: I deem your sage strategy the superior one.

sentences.zh: 」高祖大悅，賜帛三百匹、米三百石、宅一區，幷賜象笏及九環金帶，自餘什物稱是。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed three hundred bolts of silk, three hundred shi of rice, one residence, together with an ivory tablet and a nine-ring gold belt; the remaining goods were commensurate.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed three hundred bolts of silk, three hundred shi of rice, one residence, together with an ivory tablet and a nine-ring gold belt; the remaining goods were commensurate.

sentences.zh: 又詔所司給安車駟馬，隨駕入朝，幷敕所在供給。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered the relevant offices to provide a comfort carriage and four horses, that he might follow the imperial procession to court, and directed local authorities to furnish supplies.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered the relevant offices to provide a comfort carriage and four horses, that he might follow the imperial procession to court, and directed local authorities to furnish supplies.

sentences.zh: 至京，敕令于大乘佛寺參議五禮。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the capital, an edict ordered him to join deliberations on the Five Rites at Dacheng Buddhist Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the capital, an edict ordered him to join deliberations on the Five Rites at Dacheng Buddhist Temple.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，拜露門學博士、下大夫，其時年已八十餘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng he was appointed Erudite of the Lumen Academy and Lower Grand Master; at the time he was already more than eighty years old.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xuanzheng era he was appointed Erudite of the Lumen Academy and Lower Grand Master; at the time he was already more than eighty years old.

sentences.zh: 尋致仕，卒於家。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he retired and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he retired and died at home.

sentences.zh: 安生旣學為儒宗，當時受其業擅名於後者，有馬榮伯、張黑奴、竇士榮、孔籠、劉焯、劉炫等，皆其門人焉。

translations.literal: Ansheng, his learning having made him patriarch of the Confucians, had among those who received his instruction and later won fame Ma Rongbo, Zhang Heinu, Dou Shirong, Kong Long, Liu Chao, Liu Xuan, and others—all were his disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Ansheng, his learning having made him patriarch of the Confucians, had among those who received his instruction and later won fame Ma Rongbo, Zhang Heinu, Dou Shirong, Kong Long, Liu Chao, Liu Xuan, and others—all were his disciples.

sentences.zh: 所撰《周禮義疏》二十卷、《禮記義疏》四十卷、《孝經義疏》一卷，竝行於世。

translations.literal: His works Commentary and Exegesis on the Rites of Zhou in twenty juan, Commentary and Exegesis on the Record of Rites in forty juan, and Commentary and Exegesis on the Classic of Filial Piety in one juan all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works Commentary and Exegesis on the Rites of Zhou in twenty juan, Commentary and Exegesis on the Record of Rites in forty juan, and Commentary and Exegesis on the Classic of Filial Piety in one juan all circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 樂遜字遵賢，河東猗氏人也。

translations.literal: Yue Xun, courtesy name Zunxian, was a man of Yishi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Xun, whose courtesy name was Zunxian, was a native of Yishi in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 年在幼童，便有成人之操。

translations.literal: While still a child in years, he already possessed the conduct of a grown man.
translations.idiomatic: While still a child in years, he already possessed the conduct of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，為郡主簿。

translations.literal: At the capping age he served as chief clerk of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the capping age he served as chief clerk of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 魏正光中，聞碩儒徐遵明領徒趙、魏，乃就學《孝經》、《喪服》、《論語》、《詩》、《書》、《禮》、《易》、《左氏春秋》大義。

translations.literal: During Zhenguang of Wei, hearing that the great scholar Xu Zunming was leading disciples in Zhao and Wei, he went to study the essential meanings of the Classic of Filial Piety, Mourning Garments, the Analects, the Odes, the Documents, the Rites, the Changes, and the Spring and Autumn Annals of Master Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguang era of Wei, hearing that the great scholar Xu Zunming was leading disciples in Zhao and Wei, he went to study the essential meanings of the Classic of Filial Piety, Mourning Garments, the Analects, the Odes, the Documents, the Rites, the Changes, and the Spring and Autumn Annals of Master Zuo.

sentences.zh: 尋而山東寇亂，學者散逸，遜於擾攘之中，猶志道不倦。

translations.literal: Before long bandits ravaged the Shandong region and scholars scattered; amid the turmoil, Xun yet pursued the Way without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long bandits ravaged the Shandong region and scholars scattered; amid the turmoil, Xun yet pursued the Way without weariness.

sentences.zh: 永安中，釋褐安西府長流參軍。

translations.literal: During Yong'an he doffed his coarse cloth and became Chief Flowing Staff Officer of the Anxi headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yong'an era he entered official service as Chief Flowing Staff Officer of the Anxi headquarters.

sentences.zh: 大統七年，除子都督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Datong he was made Junior Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Datong era he was made Junior Commandant.

sentences.zh: 九年，太尉李弼請遜教授諸子。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Grand Commandant Li Bi requested that Xun instruct his sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, Grand Commandant Li Bi requested that Xun instruct his sons.

sentences.zh: 旣而太祖盛選賢良，授以守令。

translations.literal: Before long the Grand Ancestor extensively selected the worthy and good and appointed them as prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Grand Ancestor extensively selected the worthy and good and appointed them as prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 相府戶曹柳敏、行臺郎中盧光、河東郡丞辛粲相繼舉遜，稱有牧民之才。

translations.literal: The Household Clerk Liu Min of the chancellor's office, the Secretariat Gentleman of the traveling secretariat Lu Guang, and the Assistant Commandery Administrator Xin Can of Hedong in succession recommended Xun, declaring that he possessed the talent to govern the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Household Clerk Liu Min of the chancellor's office, the Secretariat Gentleman of the traveling secretariat Lu Guang, and the Assistant Commandery Administrator Xin Can of Hedong in succession recommended Xun, declaring that he possessed the talent to govern the people.

sentences.zh: 弼請留不遣。

translations.literal: Bi requested that he be retained and not sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi requested that he be retained and not sent away.

sentences.zh: 十六年，加授建忠將軍、左中郎將，遷輔國將軍、中散大夫、都督，歷弼府西合祭酒、功曹諮議參軍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was additionally appointed General Who Establishes Loyalty and Left Commandant of Cavalry; he was promoted to General Who Assists the State, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, and Commandant, and served successively as Libationer of the Western Pavilion of Bi's headquarters and Staff Officer for Merit Evaluation and Military Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was additionally appointed General Who Establishes Loyalty and Left Commandant of Cavalry; he was promoted to General Who Assists the State, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, and Commandant, and served successively as Libationer of the Western Pavilion of Li Bi's headquarters and Staff Officer for Merit Evaluation and Military Adviser.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，太祖召遜教授諸子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Deposed Emperor of Wei, the Grand Ancestor summoned Xun to instruct his sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Deposed Emperor of Wei, the Grand Ancestor summoned Xun to instruct his sons.

sentences.zh: 在館六年，與諸儒分授經業。

translations.literal: He remained at the academy six years, dividing the teaching of the classics with the various Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: He remained at the academy six years, dividing the teaching of the classics with the various Confucians.

sentences.zh: 遜講《孝經》、《論語》、《毛詩》及服虔所注《春秋左氏》傳。

translations.literal: Xun lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, the Mao Odes, and the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn as annotated by Fu Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Xun lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, the Mao Odes, and the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn as annotated by Fu Qian.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，授太學助教。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Imperial Academy.
