translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，以遜有理務材，除秋官府上士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, since Xun had talent for practical administration, he was made Senior Clerk of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, since Xun had talent for practical administration, he was made Senior Clerk of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 其年，治太學博士，轉治小師氏下大夫。

translations.literal: That same year he was made Erudite in charge of the Imperial Academy, then transferred to Lower Grand Master of the Junior Master Shi.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was made Erudite in charge of the Imperial Academy, then transferred to Lower Grand Master of the Junior Master Shi.

sentences.zh: 自譙王儉以下，並束脩行弟子之禮。

translations.literal: From Prince of Qiao Jian downward, all presented the silk tribute and observed the rites due a disciple.
translations.idiomatic: From Prince of Qiao Jian downward, all presented the silk tribute and observed the rites due a disciple.

sentences.zh: 遜以經術教授，甚有訓導之方。

translations.literal: Xun taught through the classical disciplines and possessed excellent methods of instruction and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Xun taught through the classical disciplines and possessed excellent methods of instruction and guidance.

sentences.zh: 及衛公直鎮蒲州，以遜為直府主簿，加車騎將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Prince Wei Zhi governed Puzhou, he made Xun chief clerk of Zhi's headquarters, with additional titles of General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Imperial Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wei Zhi governed Puzhou, he made Xun chief clerk of Zhi's headquarters, with additional titles of General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Imperial Splendor.

sentences.zh: 其一，崇治方，曰：

translations.literal: The first, exalt governance methods, it says:
translations.idiomatic: The first, exalt governance methods, it says:

sentences.zh: 竊惟今之在官者，多求清身克濟，不至惠民愛物。

translations.literal: I venture to consider that those in office today mostly seek to keep themselves upright and achieve results, yet fall short of benefiting the people and cherishing things.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to consider that those in office today mostly seek to keep themselves upright and achieve results, yet fall short of benefiting the people and cherishing things.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 比來守令年期旣促，歲責有成。

translations.literal: Recently the terms of prefects and magistrates have been short, and yearly assessments demand tangible achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the terms of prefects and magistrates have been short, and yearly assessments demand tangible achievement.

sentences.zh: 蓋謂猛濟為賢，未甚優養。

translations.literal: They generally regard fierce efficiency as excellence and scarcely show generous nurturing.
translations.idiomatic: They generally regard fierce efficiency as excellence and scarcely show generous nurturing.

sentences.zh: 此政旣代，後者復然。

translations.literal: Once this administration ends, those who follow do the same.
translations.idiomatic: Once this administration ends, those who follow do the same.

sentences.zh: 夫政之於民，過急則刻薄，傷緩則弛慢。

translations.literal: Now, when government bears upon the people, excessive urgency makes it harsh and thin, while excessive leniency makes it slack and lax.
translations.idiomatic: Now, when government bears upon the people, excessive urgency makes it harsh and thin, while excessive leniency makes it slack and lax.

sentences.zh: 是以周失舒緩，秦敗急酷。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhou perished for excessive leniency, and Qin failed for excessive severity.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Zhou perished for excessive leniency, and Qin failed for excessive severity.

sentences.zh: 民非赤子，當以赤子遇之。

translations.literal: The people are not infants, yet they should be treated as infants.
translations.idiomatic: The people are not infants, yet they should be treated as infants.

sentences.zh: 宜在舒疾得衷，不使勞擾。

translations.literal: What is fitting is that urgency and ease strike the mean, so that the people are neither toiled nor harassed.
translations.idiomatic: What is fitting is that urgency and ease strike the mean, so that the people are neither toiled nor harassed.

sentences.zh: 頃承魏之衰政，人習逋違。

translations.literal: Recently we have inherited the decayed governance of Wei, and the people are accustomed to evasion and defiance.
translations.idiomatic: Recently we have inherited the decayed governance of Wei, and the people are accustomed to evasion and defiance.

sentences.zh: 先王朝憲備行，民咸識法。

translations.literal: Under the former emperor the royal statutes were fully enforced, and the people all knew the law.
translations.idiomatic: Under the former emperor the royal statutes were fully enforced, and the people all knew the law.

sentences.zh: 但可宣風正俗，納民軌訓而已。

translations.literal: One need only spread wholesome customs, correct the mores, and bring the people into proper discipline.
translations.idiomatic: One need only spread wholesome customs, correct the mores, and bring the people into proper discipline.

sentences.zh: 自非軍旅之中，何用過為迫切。

translations.literal: Unless in military affairs, what need is there to be excessively pressing?
translations.idiomatic: Unless in military affairs, what need is there to be excessively pressing?

sentences.zh: 至於興邦致治，事由德教，漸以成之，非在倉卒。

translations.literal: As for raising the state and achieving good order, the task lies in moral instruction; it is accomplished gradually, not in haste.
translations.idiomatic: As for raising the state and achieving good order, the task lies in moral instruction; it is accomplished gradually, not in haste.

sentences.zh: 竊謂姬周盛德，治興文、武，政穆成、康。

translations.literal: I venture to say that the House of Zhou in its flourishing virtue achieved order under Kings Wen and Wu and ruled in harmony under Kings Cheng and Kang.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to say that the House of Zhou in its flourishing virtue achieved order under Kings Wen and Wu and ruled in harmony under Kings Cheng and Kang.

sentences.zh: 自斯厥後，不能無事。

translations.literal: From that time onward, no age has been without affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From that time onward, no age has been without affairs.

sentences.zh: 昔申侯將奔，楚子誨之曰「無適小國」。

translations.literal: In olden days when the Marquis of Shen was about to flee, the ruler of Chu admonished him, saying, "Do not go to a small state."
translations.idiomatic: In olden days when the Marquis of Shen was about to flee, the ruler of Chu admonished him, saying, "Do not go to a small state."

sentences.zh: 言以政狹法峻，將不汝容。

translations.literal: The meaning was that because its government was narrow and its laws severe, it would not hold you.
translations.idiomatic: The meaning was that because its government was narrow and its laws severe, it would not hold you.

sentences.zh: 敬仲入齊，稱曰「幸若獲宥，及於寬政」。

translations.literal: When Jing Zhong entered Qi, he declared, "If I am fortunate enough to be pardoned, I may reach a lenient government."
translations.idiomatic: When Jing Zhong entered Qi, he declared, "If I am fortunate enough to be pardoned, I may reach a lenient government."

sentences.zh: 然關東諸州，淪陷日久，人在塗炭，當慕息肩。

translations.literal: Yet the eastern prefectures beyond the Pass have long been lost; the people lie in fire and water and ought to yearn for rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the eastern prefectures beyond the Pass have long been lost; the people lie in fire and water and ought to yearn for rest.

sentences.zh: 若不布政優優，聞諸境外，將何以使彼勞民，歸就樂土。

translations.literal: If we do not lay forth governance that is gentle and easy, and make it known beyond our borders, how shall we cause those toiling people to return to a happy land?
translations.idiomatic: If we do not lay forth governance that is gentle and easy, and make it known beyond our borders, how shall we cause those toiling people to return to a happy land?

sentences.zh: 其二，省造作，曰：

translations.literal: The second, reduce construction work, it says:
translations.idiomatic: The second, reduce construction work, it says:

sentences.zh: 頃者魏都洛陽，一時殷盛，貴勢之家，各營第宅，車服器玩，皆尚奢靡。

translations.literal: Recently, when Wei made its capital at Luoyang, the city flourished for a time; families of noble power each built mansions, and carriages, garments, utensils, and curios all prized extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, when Wei made its capital at Luoyang, the city flourished for a time; families of noble power each built mansions, and carriages, garments, utensils, and curios all prized extravagance.

sentences.zh: 世逐浮競，人習澆薄，終使禍亂交興，天下喪敗。

translations.literal: The age pursued vain rivalry; the people grew accustomed to shallow indulgence—and in the end calamity and rebellion arose together, and the realm was lost and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The age pursued vain rivalry; the people grew accustomed to shallow indulgence—and in the end calamity and rebellion arose together, and the realm was lost and ruined.

sentences.zh: 比來朝貢，器服稍華，百工造作，務盡奇巧。

translations.literal: Recently tribute from the court has grown somewhat ornate in vessels and garments, and artisans' work strives to exhaust ingenious artistry.
translations.idiomatic: Recently tribute from the court has grown somewhat ornate in vessels and garments, and artisans' work strives to exhaust ingenious artistry.

sentences.zh: 臣誠恐物逐好移，有損政俗。

translations.literal: Your servant truly fears that when objects follow shifting tastes, governance and custom will suffer harm.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant truly fears that when objects follow shifting tastes, governance and custom will suffer harm.

sentences.zh: 如此等事，頗宜禁省。

translations.literal: Matters such as these ought largely to be forbidden and curtailed.
translations.idiomatic: Matters such as these ought largely to be forbidden and curtailed.

sentences.zh: 《記》言「無作淫巧，以蕩上心」。

translations.literal: The Record says, "Do not make licentious craftwork to unsettle the ruler's heart-mind."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says, "Do not make licentious craftwork to unsettle the ruler's heart-mind."

sentences.zh: 傳稱「宮室崇侈，民力雕弊」。

translations.literal: The Commentary records, "When palaces and chambers are grand and extravagant, the people's strength is carved away to ruin."
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary records, "When palaces and chambers are grand and extravagant, the people's strength is carved away to ruin."

sentences.zh: 漢景有云：「黃金珠玉，饑不可食，寒不可衣。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing of Han said, "Gold and pearls and jade—when hungry you cannot eat them; when cold you cannot wear them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing of Han said, "Gold and pearls and jade—when hungry you cannot eat them; when cold you cannot wear them.

sentences.zh: 」「雕文刻鏤，傷農事者也。

translations.literal: " "Elaborate carving and inlay harm the work of farming.
translations.idiomatic: " "Elaborate carving and inlay harm the work of farming.

sentences.zh: 錦繡纂組，害女功者也。

translations.literal: Brocades, embroidered silks, and braided trim harm women's work.
translations.idiomatic: Brocades, embroidered silks, and braided trim harm women's work.

sentences.zh: 」以二者為饑寒之本源矣。

translations.literal: " He took these two as the root sources of hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: " He took these two as the root sources of hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 然國家非為軍戎器用、時事要須而造者，皆徒費功力，損國害民。

translations.literal: Yet whatever the state produces that is not military equipment or what present needs require is merely wasted labor, harming the nation and injuring the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whatever the state produces that is not military equipment or what present needs require is merely wasted labor, harming the nation and injuring the people.

sentences.zh: 未如廣勸農桑，以衣食為務，使國儲豐積，大功易舉。

translations.literal: Better to encourage farming and sericulture broadly, take clothing and food as the task, let state stores accumulate in plenty, and great works will be easy to accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: Better to encourage farming and sericulture broadly, take clothing and food as the task, let state stores accumulate in plenty, and great works will be easy to accomplish.

sentences.zh: 其三，明選舉，曰：

translations.literal: The third, clarify selection and appointment, it says:
translations.idiomatic: The third, clarify selection and appointment, it says:

sentences.zh: 選曹賞錄勳賢，補擬官爵，必宜與衆共之，有明揚之授。

translations.literal: The Selection Office, in rewarding and recording meritorious worthies and in appointing to fill offices and ranks, ought to consult with the multitude and grant appointments through open commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The Selection Office, in rewarding and recording meritorious worthies and in appointing to fill offices and ranks, ought to consult with the multitude and grant appointments through open commendation.

sentences.zh: 使人得盡心，如睹白日。

translations.literal: Let people give their full devotion as if beholding the bright sun.
translations.idiomatic: Let people give their full devotion as if beholding the bright sun.

sentences.zh: 其材有升降，其功有厚薄，祿秩所加，無容不審。

translations.literal: When talent has its gradations and merit has its degrees of thickness and thinness, the salary and rank conferred must in no case fail to be examined with care.
translations.idiomatic: When talent has its gradations and merit has its degrees of thickness and thinness, the salary and rank conferred must in no case fail to be examined with care.

sentences.zh: 即如州郡選置，猶集鄉閭，況天下選曹，不取物〔望。

translations.literal: Precisely as with selection and appointment in provinces and commanderies, one still gathers hamlets and neighborhoods; how much more so the empire-wide Selection Office—one does not take public esteem [物望.
translations.idiomatic: Even provincial appointments are still made by gathering local communities; how much more, then, should the central Selection Office avoid choosing men by reputation alone?

sentences.zh: 若方〕州〔列〕郡，自可內除。

translations.literal: If it concerns] the regional provinces and [ranked] commanderies, appointments may be made from within [the bureaucracy].
translations.idiomatic: Provincial and commandery posts, at least, can be filled by internal promotion.

sentences.zh: 此外付曹銓者，旣非機事，何足可密。

translations.literal: Apart from this, what is entrusted to the Selection Office for assessment—since it is not secret affairs, why need it be confidential?
translations.idiomatic: As for other appointments handled by the personnel bureau, these are hardly state secrets—there is no reason to keep the process hidden.

sentences.zh: 人生處世，以榮祿為重，修身履行，以纂身為名。

translations.literal: In human life and conduct in the world, honor and salary weigh heavily; in cultivating the self and fulfilling conduct, one takes establishing the person as one's name.
translations.idiomatic: Men live in this world with glory and emolument as what they value most, and they build reputation through self-cultivation and upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 然逢時旣難，失時為易。

translations.literal: Yet meeting the right time is already difficult; missing the right time is easy.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing the right moment is hard; letting it slip away is all too easy.

sentences.zh: 其選置之日，宜令衆心明白，然後呈奏。

translations.literal: On the day of selection and appointment, one ought to make the hearts of the multitude clear, and only then present the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When selections are made, the public should understand the grounds for each appointment before the list is submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 使功勤見知，品物稱悅。

translations.literal: Thus making merit and diligence be seen and known, and all things declare satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: So that merit and diligence receive recognition and everyone finds the outcome fair and pleasing.

sentences.zh: 其四，重戰伐，曰：

translations.literal: The fourth: emphasize warfare and campaigns, it says:
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, on giving due weight to military action, he wrote:

sentences.zh: 魏祚告終，天睠在德。

translations.literal: The Wei fortune reached its end; Heaven's favor rests on virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Wei has run its course, and Heaven now favors the virtuous.

sentences.zh: 而高洋稱僭，先迷未敗，擁逼山東，事切肘腋。

translations.literal: Yet Gao Yang declared himself [ emperor beyond his station ], first deluded though not yet defeated, pressing upon Shandong—the matter presses close to the armpit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gao Yang has seized the imperial title; though still unchecked, he already presses on Shandong—a threat right at our side.

sentences.zh: 譬猶棋劫相持，爭行先後。

translations.literal: It is like a life-and-death grip in weiqi, contending over who moves first.
translations.idiomatic: It is like a critical struggle over territory on the board, where each side fights to seize the initiative.

sentences.zh: 若一行非當，或成彼利。

translations.literal: If one move is not appropriate, it may become the other's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: A single misstep could hand the enemy his opening.

sentences.zh: 誠應舍小營大，先保封域，不宜貪利在邊，輕為興動。

translations.literal: Truly one ought to relinquish the small and plan for the large, first secure the territorial boundaries—not appropriate to be greedy for gains at the border and lightly launch campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: We should sacrifice minor gains for major strategy: secure our borders first, rather than chasing frontier profits with rash military action.

sentences.zh: 捷則勞兵分守，敗則所損已多。

translations.literal: If victorious, then troops are wearied and split for garrison duty; if defeated, the losses are already great.
translations.idiomatic: Victory would still leave us straining to garrison conquered ground; defeat would cost far too much.

sentences.zh: 國家雖強，洋不受弱。

translations.literal: Though the state is strong, Yang will not accept being weak.
translations.idiomatic: Our realm may be powerful, but Gao Yang is not a man who will yield to weakness.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「德則不競，何憚於病！

translations.literal: The Odes says: "With virtue one does not contend—what fear of affliction!
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says, "When virtue is supreme, there is no need to compete—so why dread hardship?

sentences.zh: 」唯德可以庇民，非恃彊也。

translations.literal: " Only virtue can shelter the people; it is not reliance on strength.
translations.idiomatic: Only virtue can truly protect the people—not brute force.

sentences.zh: 夫力均勢敵，則進德者勝。

translations.literal: Now when strength is equal and power matched, then the one who advances in virtue wins.
translations.idiomatic: When two powers are evenly matched, the side that cultivates virtue prevails.

sentences.zh: 君子道長，則小人道消。

translations.literal: When the way of the gentleman lengthens, the way of the petty man wanes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Way of the noble man gains ground, the way of the base man retreats.

sentences.zh: 故昔之善戰者，先為不可勝，以待敵之可勝。

translations.literal: Therefore those skilled in warfare in antiquity first made themselves impossible to defeat, then awaited the enemy's becoming possible to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient masters of war first made themselves invincible, then waited for the enemy to expose a weakness.

sentences.zh: 彼行暴戾，我則寬仁。

translations.literal: They act with violence and cruelty; we then are lenient and humane.
translations.idiomatic: Let them rule with cruelty; we shall respond with clemency and benevolence.

sentences.zh: 彼為刻薄，我必惠化。

translations.literal: They practice harshness and stringency; we must use gracious transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Where they govern harshly, we must govern with generous kindness.

sentences.zh: 使德澤旁流，人思有道。

translations.literal: Make virtue and grace flow on every side; people will think upon the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Let our virtue spread in every direction until the people themselves yearn for righteous rule.

sentences.zh: 然後觀釁而作，可以集事。

translations.literal: Then observing the opening to act, one can gather affairs to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Only then, watching for the right opening, can we strike and achieve our aim.

sentences.zh: 其五，禁奢侈，曰：

translations.literal: The fifth: prohibit extravagance, it says:
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, on prohibiting luxury, he wrote:

sentences.zh: 按禮，人有貴賤，物有等差，使用之有節，品類之有度。

translations.literal: According to ritual, people have noble and base ranks, things have gradations; in use there are limits, in categories there are measures.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual prescribes that people differ in rank and things differ in grade; consumption must observe proper limits and each category its proper measure.

sentences.zh: 馬后為天下母，而身服大練，所以率下也。

translations.literal: Empress Ma was mother to all under Heaven, yet she personally wore coarse hemp—it was thereby to lead those below.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ma, though mother of the realm, wore only plain cloth herself—she meant to set an example for her subjects.

sentences.zh: 季孫相三君矣，家無衣帛之妾，所以勵俗也。

translations.literal: Ji Sun served as prime minister to three rulers, yet his household had no concubines clothed in silk—it was thereby to encourage custom.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sun, who had served three Lu rulers as chief minister, kept no silk-clad concubines in his household—he sought to reform public morals by example.

sentences.zh: 比來富貴之家，為意稍廣，無不資裝婢隸，作車後容儀，服飾華美，昡曜街衢。

translations.literal: Recently among wealthy and noble households, their intentions have grown somewhat broad; none fail to outfit maidservants and slaves, arrange the ceremonial display behind their carriages, dress in splendid finery, and dazzle the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the great houses have grown ever more extravagant: they deck out servants, parade retinues behind their carriages, and dress in gorgeous clothes that blaze through the streets.

sentences.zh: 仍使行者輟足，路人傾蓋。

translations.literal: They still make travelers halt their feet and passersby tilt their carriage covers.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers stop in their tracks and onlookers crane their necks to stare.

sentences.zh: 論其輸力公家，未若介冑之士；

translations.literal: Speaking of their contribution of strength to the public house, they do not compare to men in armor and helm;
translations.idiomatic: Measured by what they contribute to the state, they cannot compare with armored soldiers;

sentences.zh: 然其坐受優賞，自踰攻戰之人。

translations.literal: yet they sit and receive lavish rewards, themselves exceeding those who fought in battle.
translations.idiomatic: yet they sit at ease and collect generous rewards that surpass what fighting men receive.

sentences.zh: 縱令不惜功費，豈不有虧厥德。

translations.literal: Even if one does not begrudge the labor and expense, would it not still diminish that virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Even if one can afford the waste, does it not still erode one's moral standing?

sentences.zh: 必有儲蓄之餘，孰與務恤軍士。

translations.literal: If there must be surplus in store, who is better served by devoting care to soldiers?
translations.idiomatic: Surely any surplus in the treasury would be better spent caring for the troops.

sentences.zh: 魯莊公有云：「衣食所安，不敢愛也，必以分人。

translations.literal: Duke Zhuang of Lu said: "The food and clothing in which I find comfort—I dare not hoard them; I must share them with others.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhuang of Lu said, "The food and clothing that sustain me I dare not keep to myself; I must share them with others.

sentences.zh: 」《詩》言：「豈曰無衣，與子同袍。

translations.literal: " The Odes states: "How can it be said we have no clothes? I will share my robe with you.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says, "Are we not clothed? I will share my robe with you.

sentences.zh: 」皆所以取人力也。

translations.literal: " All this is to win men's labor.
translations.idiomatic: All such examples show how to win men's willing effort.

sentences.zh: 又陳事上議之徒，亦應不少，當有上徹天聽者。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who present memorials with proposals to the throne should not be few; there ought to be those whose words penetrate Heaven's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Many others must also be submitting policy memorials; surely some of their words reach Your Majesty's ears.

sentences.zh: 未聞是非。

translations.literal: I have not heard whether they were approved or rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one never hears whether they were accepted or dismissed.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖念存物議，欲盡天下之情，而天下之情猶為未盡。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, though bearing in mind preserving public discussion and wishing to exhaust all feelings under Heaven, the feelings under Heaven are still not fully [heard].
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty may wish to preserve open debate and hear every voice in the realm, yet the realm's voices are still not fully heard.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 取人受言，貴在顯用。

translations.literal: In receiving men and accepting words, what is precious is manifest employment.
translations.idiomatic: When you heed advice, what matters is to act on it openly.

sentences.zh: 若納而不顯，是而不用，則言之者或寡矣。

translations.literal: If one accepts but does not display, approves but does not use, then those who speak may grow few.
translations.idiomatic: If you approve memorials in private but never put them into practice, fewer and fewer people will speak up.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，以訓導有方，頻加賞賜。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, because his instruction and guidance had method, he was repeatedly granted rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding, he received repeated rewards for his effective teaching.

sentences.zh: 遷遂伯中大夫，授驃騎將軍、大都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Baron of Sui, Grand Master of the Palace, and granted General Who Spreads Majestic Might and Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Baron of Sui, Grand Master of the Palace, and appointed General Who Spreads Majestic Might and Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 四年，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was advanced to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Preceptors.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry with rank equal to the Three Preceptors.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔魯公贇、畢公賢等，俱以束修之禮，同受業焉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict ordered the Duke of Lu, Yun, the Duke of Bi, Xian, and others all to receive instruction together with the teacher's-gift ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the throne commanded the Duke of Lu, Yun, the Duke of Bi, Xian, and others to become his pupils with the formal ceremony of the teacher's gift.

sentences.zh: 天和元年，岐州刺史、陳公純舉遜為賢良。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianhe, the Prefect of Qi Province, the Duke of Chen, Chun, recommended Yue Xun as a worthy and good man.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianhe, the Duke of Chen, Chun, as Prefect of Qi Province, recommended Yue Xun as a man of talent and virtue.

sentences.zh: 五年，遜以年在懸車，上表致仕，優詔不許。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Yue Xun, his years having reached the age of the suspended carriage, submitted a memorial to retire; a gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Yue Xun petitioned to retire, having reached the age of seventy; a gracious edict refused his request.

sentences.zh: 於是賜以粟帛及錢等，授湖州刺史，封安邑縣子，邑四百戶。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was granted grain, silk, money, and the like, appointed Prefect of Hu Province, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Anyi County with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was then granted grain, silk, and money, appointed Prefect of Hu Province, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Anyi with four hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 民多蠻左，未習儒風。

translations.literal: The people were mostly Man tribes of the left, not accustomed to Confucian ways.
translations.idiomatic: The population was largely non-Han tribes who had not yet adopted Confucian culture.

sentences.zh: 遜勸勵生徒，加以課試，數年之間，化洽州境。

translations.literal: Yue Xun encouraged and urged students, added examinations and tests, and within several years transformation pervaded the prefecture's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Xun encouraged his students, instituted examinations, and within a few years transformed the entire prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蠻俗生子，長大多與父母別居。

translations.literal: In barbarian custom, when sons were born and grew up, most lived apart from their parents.
translations.idiomatic: By local custom, sons who came of age usually moved out and lived apart from their parents.

sentences.zh: 遜每加勸導，多革前弊。

translations.literal: Yue Xun repeatedly added encouragement and guidance, reforming many former abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Xun repeatedly counseled them and abolished many old harmful practices.

sentences.zh: 在任數載，頻被褒錫。

translations.literal: During several years in office, he was repeatedly praised and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Over several years in office he received frequent commendations and gifts.

sentences.zh: 秩滿還朝，拜皇太子諫議，復在露門教授皇子，增邑一百戶。

translations.literal: When his term was complete he returned to court, was appointed Remonstrating Advisor to the Crown Prince, again taught princes at the Lum Gate, and his fief was increased by one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned to court as Remonstrating Advisor to the Crown Prince, resumed teaching princes at the Lum Gate, and received an additional hundred households in his fief.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，進位上儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng, he was advanced in rank to Grand General with Upper Equal in Honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanzheng he was promoted to Grand General with the highest honorary rank.

sentences.zh: 大象初，進爵崇業郡公，增邑通前二千戶，又為露門博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daxiang, he was advanced in noble rank to Duke of Chongye Commandery, his fief increased to two thousand households counting all previous grants, and he again served as Erudite of the Lum Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Daxiang era he was made Duke of Chongye Commandery with a total fief of two thousand households and again appointed Erudite of the Lum Gate.

sentences.zh: 二年，進位開府儀同

translations.literal: In the second year, he was advanced in rank to Generalissimo of the Government, Equal in Honor to
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to Generalissimo with an office equal in honor to the

sentences.zh: （三司）

translations.literal: (the Three Preceptors)
translations.idiomatic: Three Preceptors

sentences.zh: 大將軍，出為汾陰郡守。

translations.literal: Grand General, and sent out as Administrator of Fenyin Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General, and was appointed Administrator of Fenyin Commandery.

sentences.zh: 遜以老病固辭，詔許之。

translations.literal: Yue Xun firmly declined on grounds of old age and illness; an edict granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Xun firmly declined on account of age and illness, and the throne granted his request.

sentences.zh: 乃改授東揚州刺史，仍賜安車、衣服及奴婢等。

translations.literal: He was then reassigned as Prefect of Eastern Yang Province, and still granted a comfortable carriage, clothing, and slave girls and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He was instead appointed Prefect of Eastern Yang Province and given a comfortable carriage, robes, and attendants.

sentences.zh: 又于本郡賜田十頃。

translations.literal: Also in his home commandery he was granted ten qing of farmland.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted ten qing of farmland in his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 儒者以為榮。

translations.literal: Confucian scholars regarded it as honor.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian scholars considered this a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇元年，卒於家，年八十二。

translations.literal: In the first year of Sui Kaihuang, he died at home, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang under the Sui he died at home at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加蒲、陝二州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted his former office, with the addition of Prefect of the two provinces of Pu and Shan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his former rank plus the titles of Prefect of Pu and Prefect of Shan.

sentences.zh: 遜性柔謹，寡於交遊。

translations.literal: Yue Xun's nature was gentle and careful; he had few social connections.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Xun was gentle and cautious by nature and kept few close associates.

sentences.zh: 立身以忠信為本，不自矜尚。

translations.literal: In establishing himself he took loyalty and trustworthiness as root, not self-exalting.
translations.idiomatic: He grounded his conduct in loyalty and trustworthiness and never put himself forward.

sentences.zh: 每在衆中，言論未嘗為人之先。

translations.literal: Whenever among a crowd, in speech he never was ahead of others.
translations.idiomatic: In company he never spoke before others.

sentences.zh: 學者以此稱之。

translations.literal: Scholars praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Men of learning admired him for this restraint.

sentences.zh: 所著《孝經》、《論語》、《毛詩》、《左氏春秋序論》十餘篇。

translations.literal: He authored more than ten pieces including "Preface Discussions" on the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, the Mao Odes, and the Zuoshi Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote more than ten works, including preface essays on the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, the Mao Odes, and the Zuoshi Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 又著《春秋序義》，通賈、服說，發杜氏違，辭理竝可觀。

translations.literal: He also authored "Preface to the Meaning of the Spring and Autumn," incorporating the explanations of Jia and Fu, exposing the errors of the Du clan; in wording and reasoning both are worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Preface to the Meaning of the Spring and Autumn, drawing on the commentaries of Jia Kui and Fu Qian while exposing flaws in Du Yu's readings—a work admirable in both style and argument.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：前世通六藝之士，莫不兼達政術，故云拾青紫如地芥。

translations.literal: The historian says: scholars of former ages who mastered the Six Arts—none failed also to reach proficiency in statecraft; hence it was said that picking up purple and blue rank was like mustard plants on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: in earlier times, men who mastered the Six Arts invariably understood statecraft as well; people said that winning high office was as easy as picking up plants from the ground.

sentences.zh: 近代守一經之儒，多暗於時務，故有貧且賤之恥。

translations.literal: Confucians of recent times who kept to one classic were mostly dark regarding affairs of the age; hence the shame of poverty and baseness.
translations.idiomatic: Recent scholars who clung to a single classic were often ignorant of practical affairs, and so suffered the disgrace of poverty and obscurity.

sentences.zh: 雖通塞有命，而大抵皆然。

translations.literal: Though success and obstruction have fate, broadly speaking all were thus.
translations.idiomatic: Though fortune and misfortune may be ordained, this was broadly the pattern.

sentences.zh: 嘗論之曰：夫金之質也至剛，鑄之可以成器；

translations.literal: Once he discussed it, saying: Now the substance of gold is utmost hard; cast, it can become a vessel;
translations.idiomatic: He once observed: gold is by nature the hardest of metals, yet cast in a mold it becomes a useful vessel;

sentences.zh: 水之性也柔弱，壅之可以壞山。

translations.literal: the nature of water is soft and yielding; dammed, it can destroy mountains.
translations.idiomatic: water is by nature soft and yielding, yet dammed up it can wear down a mountain.

sentences.zh: 況乎肖天地之貌，含五常之德，朱藍易染，熏蕕可變，固以隨鄒俗而好長纓，化齊風而貴紫服。

translations.literal: How much more so for those who emulate Heaven and Earth's appearance and contain the virtue of the Five Constants—vermillion and indigo are easily dyed, fragrant grass and foul grass can be changed; thus following Zou custom they love long cap-tassels, transformed by Qi wind they prize purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: How much more true of human beings, who share the form of Heaven and Earth and embody the Five Constants: like cloth that takes crimson or indigo dye, like character shaped by good or foul influence—men follow the customs of Zou and prize official insignia, then adopt Qi fashions and value purple robes.

sentences.zh: 若乃進趣矜尚，中庸之常情；

translations.literal: As for advancing in ambition and self-exaltation, it is the ordinary sentiment of the Mean;
translations.idiomatic: Ambition and self-regard are ordinary human feelings—the very heart of the Doctrine of the Mean;

sentences.zh: 高秩厚禮，上智之所欲。

translations.literal: high rank and thick rewards are what superior minds desire.
translations.idiomatic: high rank and generous rewards are what the wisest men naturally seek.

sentences.zh: 是以兩漢之朝，重經術而輕律令。

translations.literal: Therefore in the courts of the Two Han dynasties, classical learning was weighted heavily and law codes lightly.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the Han dynasties valued classical learning above legal expertise.

sentences.zh: 其聰明特達者，咸勵精於專門。

translations.literal: Those who were brilliantly exceptional all devoted their refinement to a specialized school.
translations.idiomatic: The most gifted devoted themselves wholeheartedly to a single discipline.

sentences.zh: 以通賢之質，挾黼藻之美，大則必至公卿，小則不失守令。

translations.literal: With talent penetrating sagehood and bearing elegant literary ornament, the great necessarily reached ministers and chief counselors; the lesser did not fail to become prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Armed with genuine talent and polished literary accomplishment, the best rose to the highest offices and even the lesser among them became prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 近代之政，先法令而後經術。

translations.literal: In recent government, law codes come first and classical learning after.
translations.idiomatic: Recent regimes have put law codes first and classical learning second.

sentences.zh: 其沉默孤微者，亦篤志於章句，以先王之道，飾腐儒之姿，達則不過侍講訓冑，窮則終於弊衣簞食。

translations.literal: Those who are silent and isolated and obscure also devote their will to commentarial clauses, using the Way of the former kings to adorn the appearance of pedantic scholars; when successful they reach no further than lecturing and instructing the crown prince's sons, when poor they end in patched clothes and bamboo rice.
translations.idiomatic: The obscure scholar buries himself in textual glosses, draping the pedant's mantle in the language of the sages; if he succeeds he becomes no more than a tutor to the imperial heirs, and if he fails he dies in patched clothes with nothing but coarse fare.

sentences.zh: 由斯言之，非兩漢棟樑之所育，近代薪樗之所產哉，蓋好尚之道殊，遭遇之時異也。

translations.literal: From this speaking, are they not pillars nurtured by the Two Han, but firewood and stink-elm produced by recent times? It is simply that the ways of preference differ and the times of encounter differ.
translations.idiomatic: In other words, it is not that Han times bred pillars of state while our age produces only firewood—the difference lies in what the age values and what opportunities it offers.

sentences.zh: 史臣每聞故老，稱沈重所學，非止《六經》而已。

translations.literal: The historian, whenever he heard old men, praised Shen Zhong's learning as not stopping at the Six Classics alone.
translations.idiomatic: The historian often heard elders say that Shen Zhong's learning extended far beyond the Six Classics.

sentences.zh: 至於天官、律曆、陰陽、緯候，流畧所載，釋老之典，靡不博綜，窮其幽賾。

translations.literal: As for the Offices of Heaven, calendar and computation, yin and yang, weft apocrypha and portents, what the Liulue records, and the canons of Buddhism and Daoism—none were not broadly synthesized, their hidden depths exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered astronomy, calendrical science, yin-yang theory, apocryphal texts, the Liulue treatises, and the scriptures of Buddhism and Daoism, plumbing each to its deepest reaches.

sentences.zh: 故能馳聲海內，為一代儒宗。

translations.literal: Therefore he could gallop in fame within the seas, becoming the Confucian patriarch of a generation.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation spread throughout the realm, and he became the leading Confucian scholar of his age.

sentences.zh: 雖前世徐廣、何承天之儔，不足過也。

translations.literal: Though the peers of former ages, Xu Guang and He Chengtian, were not enough to surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: Even such earlier masters as Xu Guang and He Chengtian could not match him.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou as the base for collation.
translations.idiomatic: This edition was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou (November 1971).
